title: Haiti’s hunger crisis is projected to deepen
summary: The IPC estimates that 5.94 million people face crisis-level hunger or worse during September 2026–February 2027. Its projection rises to 6.35 million for March–June 2027. Insecurity, displacement, high food prices and climate shocks are driving the outlook.

photo.label: ARCHIVE PHOTO · AUGUST 2021
photo.caption: Archive: residents gather for a U.S. Navy food delivery in Saint-Louis-du-Sud, Haiti, on 28 August 2021 during relief efforts after the August 2021 earthquake. This photograph does not show the current hunger crisis.
photo.credit: U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class John Bellino/Released
photo.alt: Boxes of emergency food in a field as a large crowd waits in the distance in Saint-Louis-du-Sud during Haiti's 2021 earthquake response.
photo.homeCaption: 2021 earthquake food relief, Saint-Louis-du-Sud. Not the current hunger crisis.

title: Sudan’s damaged power network puts essential care at risk
summary: The UN says strikes on Sudan’s energy infrastructure are disrupting water and hospital care. Its nearly $2.9 billion humanitarian appeal was 47% funded on November 4.

title: Fighting in eastern Congo is closing classrooms
summary: The UN reports that fighting in Uvira territory has closed 26 primary schools, affecting nearly 6,000 children. Violence is also displacing families and obstructing aid.

title: Climate preparedness faces a major funding shortfall
summary: UNEP estimates developing countries will need about $305 billion a year for climate adaptation by 2035. Even the ambition to triple international public adaptation finance would cover only 20–29% of estimated needs, the agency says.

title: Millions of children remain outside formal education
summary: UNICEF and UNESCO report that 53% of primary-school-age children in Afghanistan are outside formal general education. Their report also says more than 2.6 million girls have been denied secondary education since 2021.

photo.alt: A wide view of pupils seated in a classroom at Aliabad School near Mazar-e-Sharif, Afghanistan, photographed in March 2012.

title: Displacement and rising prices squeeze families in Yemen
summary: The UN reports nearly 310,000 people displaced in Yemen since early August. Disrupted transport has driven up prices in Taiz; many families still need shelter.
